title: 🗳️ Susan Kim · Council · inc
text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3cfe245ae5f3818bbdb4ce3dded96e5f as of 2026-09-02T22:40:06.456Z: {"title":"Susan Kim · Council · inc"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🗳️"} **Filled card. Not published.** Susan Kim · Council · incumbent. Scored 2 Sep 2026 against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)** using the 12-topic template and Decision 14. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom and is Joa's to apply or reject. **Pass 2, 2 Sep 2026.** Second evidence sweep added a per-councillor roll-call source that pass 1 did not have (Vote Ready Victoria), plus Kim's own 2026 verbatim quotes and a completed 2026 housing questionnaire. **n moved from 4 to 17.** Three rulings are open and flagged in Working notes; none of them changes the proposed live letter. ## What changed in this pass
# Change Why
1 **13 new scored cells** from named roll-call votes 2022–26 Pass 1 had no per-councillor vote source. [votereadyvictoria.ca](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/) publishes named for/against lists for every non-unanimous vote of this term.
2 **M66 quote corrected.** Pass 1 carried a paraphrase ("the tax hike was simply not enough") The sourced verbatim is "It's so funny to me that we're at each other's throats about this when the system itself is just flawed. We're being asked to tax in a way that just sucks." Vote date confirmed **7 May 2026**.
3 **Kim-owned 2026 sentences located** (two, Victoria Buzz 17 Aug 2026) Pass 1 concluded there were none. Both are campaign-framing, not policy instruments, so neither scores. Recorded anyway.
4 **6 cells moved from — to 📋 Record** A sourced vote that does not touch the Program's instrument is Record, shown not scored. Better than a bare dash: the voter sees the fact.
5 **Completed 2026 housing questionnaire found** (Homes for Living) Answers are not published. The ranking itself is a third-party assessment and **is not a source**. Logged as a retrieval target.
6 **Two template gaps found:** M20 and M45 have no cell in the 55 Same class of gap as M83. Kim has a sourced vote on each. Not scored until a row exists.
## Card
Field Value
Name Susan Kim (김수잔)
Office Council (also seeking CRD Director)
Kind inc (held City office 2022–26 — Record in the cell; a sourced miss caps that cell below Close)
Platform URL (2026) No Kim-owned 2026 platform page. [https://www.susankim.ca/](https://www.susankim.ca/) did not resolve on either pass. Slate [https://www.victoriaforall.ca/](https://www.victoriaforall.ca/) is her only campaign site and is written as *we*.
Platform lastmod n/a — no Kim-owned page. Slate site carries no lastmod.
Retrieved 2026-09-02 (two sweeps)
Scored answers (measures with an answer) **17 / 55**
Record lines 📋 (shown, not scored) **6**
Letter (only at 5 scored answers: B+, B, C, D, or —) **—** · awaiting Joa's click. n = 17, threshold met. Internal proposal at the bottom.
Checked by · date Verifier · 2026-09-02 (pass 2)
### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **record** Voted NO on the 7.28% aggregate / 9.34% residential 2026 budget because it was too low: "It's so funny to me that we're at each other's throats about this when the system itself is just flawed. We're being asked to tax in a way that just sucks." Also voted NO on the Nov 2025 reduction that would have held the increase to 4%. [https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/2026-budget-reductions/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/2026-budget-reductions/) votes 26 Nov 2025 and 7 May 2026 / press 11 May 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
Downtown order M26 / M27 **record** Lone NO on the daytime-sheltering enforcement motion, 8–1. Voted YES on formalising the overnight-sheltering ban in Topaz, Hollywood and Regatta Point parks. No Public Order Team or bylaw-hours position in any 2026 text. [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-calls-for-stepped-up-effort-to-halt-sheltering-on-streets-9240701](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-calls-for-stepped-up-effort-to-halt-sheltering-on-streets-9240701) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/parks-regulation-bylaw-amendment-sheltering-restrictions/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/parks-regulation-bylaw-amendment-sheltering-restrictions/) votes 2 Nov 2023 and 18 Jul 2024 / press 19 Jul 2024, retrieved 2026-09-02
Housing M6 **record** Named YES on Missing Middle (6–3), on the Delegation Bylaw aligning land use with provincial housing statutes (8–1), on the Official Community Plan (5–3), and on reducing minimum parking requirements (6–3). No Kim-owned 2026 housing sentence. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/missing-middle-housing-initiative-policy/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/missing-middle-housing-initiative-policy/) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-adopts-divisive-missing-middle-housing-program-6443676](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-adopts-divisive-missing-middle-housing-program-6443676) votes 26 Jan 2023, 13 May 2024, 31 Aug 2025, 2 Oct 2025 / press 27 Jan 2023, retrieved 2026-09-02
Household bill M66d **—** Water, sewer, stormwater and a combined household number appear in no Kim-owned or slate 2026 text. — —
Written program — **—** No Kim-owned 2026 program. [susankim.ca](http://susankim.ca) did not resolve on either sweep. The slate site is her only campaign platform and is written as *we*. She did complete a 2026 housing questionnaire, but the answers are not published. [https://www.victoriaforall.ca/](https://www.victoriaforall.ca/) · [https://www.homesforliving.ca/elections/victoria](https://www.homesforliving.ca/elections/victoria) retrieved 2026-09-02
--- ## The 12 topics No topic gets its own letter. Area columns stay blank. Rules as written on . A dash is unknown, not a fail. 📋 Record is shown, not scored, and does not add to n. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition **Close 2.0** Four named supply votes. Missing Middle 6–3: the policy "up-zones single-family residential lots to allow townhouses, triplexes, and houseplexes to be built without going through the council rezoning or public hearing process." Plus Delegation Bylaw 8–1, OCP 5–3, parking-minimum reduction 6–3. Commits + comparable instrument: real supply, not M6's composition shares or quarterly target reporting. No sourced miss on this cell. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/missing-middle-housing-initiative-policy/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/missing-middle-housing-initiative-policy/) vote 26 Jan 2023 / press 27 Jan 2023, retrieved 2026-09-02
2 M6b land bank + co-ops — No Kim-owned sentence and no sourced vote on a City land bank, an acquisition fund or a non-profit right of first refusal. Slate promises "build public and co-operative housing" and doubled spending; that is *we*, held under Ruling 1 below. — —
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening **Close 2.0** YES on the Delegation Bylaw, 8–1: council "adopts the Delegation Bylaw and updated associated land-use bylaws" to "better align its land-use regulations with provincial housing statutes that were enacted to speed up the pace of homebuilding." Commits + comparable: a genuine approval-speed instrument. No published category benchmarks, which is the other half of M7. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/city-council-adopts-delegation-bylaw/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/city-council-adopts-delegation-bylaw/) vote 13 May 2024, retrieved 2026-09-02
4 M7b pattern-book housing — No pre-approved standard-design or expedited-stream position in any Kim-owned text or sourced vote. — —
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty **Close 2.0** YES 8–1 on the DCC waiver: "Council approves a new grant policy that offsets the City's Development Cost Charges (DCCs) for eligible below-market housing projects." M8's named instrument is "targeted DCC reductions." Comparable rather than same: hers is below-market rather than purpose-built rental, and carries no published infrastructure funding plan. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/development-cost-charge-waiver-for-affordable-housing-providers-policy/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/development-cost-charge-waiver-for-affordable-housing-providers-policy/) vote 16 Nov 2024, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team — No position on a co-located Downtown Public Order Team in any Kim-owned text or sourced vote. — —
7 M26b civilian crisis response **Weak 0.5** On the Feb 2025 police-staffing vote she advocated redirecting funds "toward alternative services like housing, social support programs, harm reduction efforts, and mental health resources." Agrees on the goal, names no instrument: no crisis-response capacity, no published dispatch criteria, no diversion figure. The slate's "24-hour mental health crisis response" is *we*, held under Ruling 1. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/victoria-police-staffing/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/victoria-police-staffing/) vote 27 Feb 2025, retrieved 2026-09-02
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — No bylaw-enforcement-hours position in any Kim-owned text or sourced vote. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement — No position on chronic-disorder data targeting. — —
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws **Opposed −1.0** "Coun. Susan Kim, the lone vote against the motion" on stepped-up daytime sheltering enforcement, 8–1: "It's just not enough because I don't believe that the deus ex machina we're waiting for is going to come." The tracker records her argument that accelerating enforcement was a band-aid that would "simply disperse vulnerable people and disconnect them from critical social and health services." A recorded vote against the cell's own instrument. [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-calls-for-stepped-up-effort-to-halt-sheltering-on-streets-9240701](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-calls-for-stepped-up-effort-to-halt-sheltering-on-streets-9240701) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/daytime-sheltering-enforcement-motion/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/daytime-sheltering-enforcement-motion/) vote 18 Jul 2024 / press 19 Jul 2024, retrieved 2026-09-02
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) — No position on buffer zones around child-focused spaces. — —
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting **Close 2.0** YES 8–1 on "formally implementing the official bylaw change … of banning overnight sheltering at Topaz Park, Hollywood Park, and Regatta Point Park," and YES 7–2 on permanently prohibiting overnight sheltering in those parks "conditional on finding alternative housing options for the occupants." Commits + comparable: park-specific prohibitions rather than M34's rapid-removal protocol. Her daytime-enforcement NO is scored on row 10 and shown here as context only. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/parks-regulation-bylaw-amendment-sheltering-restrictions/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/parks-regulation-bylaw-amendment-sheltering-restrictions/) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/three-parks-without-overnight-sheltering/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/three-parks-without-overnight-sheltering/) votes 2 Nov 2023 and 6 Jul 2023 per tracker, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) **Opposed −1.0** "It's so funny to me that we're at each other's throats about this when the system itself is just flawed. We're being asked to tax in a way that just sucks." Voted NO on the 2026 budget (7.28% aggregate, 9.34% residential) on the ground that the increase was too low, and NO in Nov 2025 on reducing infrastructure funding "from \$5.5 million to \$4 million to help cap the city's property tax increase at 4%." Two recorded votes against a residential-rate cap. [https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/2026-budget-reductions/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/2026-budget-reductions/) votes 26 Nov 2025 and 7 May 2026 / press 11 May 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule — No position on returning over-collection or on a debt rule. — —
15 M66d the Household Bill — Water, sewer, stormwater and a combined published household number appear nowhere. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger **Partial 1.0** YES 7–2: council "voted to urge BC Housing and Island Health to provide supportive housing and treatment for individuals sleeping downtown, citing an emergency." Also YES 7–2 on requesting stable provincial active-transportation funding, 15 Jun 2026. Commits, but neither instrument: no quarterly downloading ledger, no twice-yearly UBCM/FCM resolutions, no published refusal threshold. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/provincial-support-for-housing-treatment/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/provincial-support-for-housing-treatment/) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/request-for-stable-provincial-active-transportation-funding/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/request-for-stable-provincial-active-transportation-funding/) votes 26 Jun 2025 and 15 Jun 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — She sits on the Regional Water Supply Commission (2025–2026) and is seeking a CRD Director seat, but **holding a seat is not a source**. No published position on the regional bill or a CRD reporting duty. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office **Close 2.0** YES 7–2, 25 Jul 2026: council "supported measures to encourage new hotel construction in the central business district, including increased non-residential density and temporary property-tax exemption for qualifying hotels." Commits + comparable: a real tax-base and tourism instrument inside the campaign year, but not M71's storefront-vacancy target or M73b's single mandate. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/hotel-development-density-and-tax-incentives-policy/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/hotel-development-density-and-tax-incentives-policy/) vote 25 Jul 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — The Aug 2025 parking package included "reviewing metered parking," which raises the topic without a goal or an action. Mentions is a dash and does not resolve up. First-hour free is not a Year 1 instrument in the Program. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. — No sentence and no sourced vote on government-to-government working tables, Indigenous procurement, lək̓ʷəŋən place names, cultural protocols or a services liaison. Professional background and the slate's decolonization language are not a source. — —
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) **Aligned 3.0** YES 7–2 on the Displaced Tenant Assistance Compensation policy, and part of the unanimous 30 Jul 2026 council decision raising moving-expense compensation for long-term tenants displaced by redevelopment. M9's named instrument is "moving-cost compensation indexed to local rents." Commits + same instrument, inside the campaign year. No sourced miss on this cell. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/displaced-tenant-assistance-compensation-policy/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/displaced-tenant-assistance-compensation-policy/) · [https://cheknews.ca/renovicted-tenants-in-victoria-will-get-more-compensation-1339867/](https://cheknews.ca/renovicted-tenants-in-victoria-will-get-more-compensation-1339867/) votes 15 May 2025 and 30 Jul 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists — No position on a digital, rules-based allocation system. — —
23 M11 Housing First + STEP throughput **Close 2.0** YES 6–3 on a "permanent 40-unit supportive housing facility at 225 Russell Street"; YES 6–3 on zoning "allowing temporary social-services centres and shelters to operate in any city neighbourhood without undergoing a site-specific public rezoning process"; YES 6–2 on \$100,000 stop-gap funding for Our Place Society. Commits + comparable: the Housing First siting half is there, the STEP throughput and published cost-per-placement half is not. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/russell-street-supportive-housing-facility/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/russell-street-supportive-housing-facility/) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/temporary-shelters-supportive-services-zoning/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/temporary-shelters-supportive-services-zoning/) votes 16 Mar 2024, 24 May 2024, 25 Jul 2024 per tracker, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 6 · Families
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
24 M12/M13b/M13c childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is \$0 → M13d) — She is City of Victoria Youth Council Liaison (2025–2026), but **holding a seat is not a source**. No sourced action on childcare spaces, doctor recruitment or an 18–25 strategy. 2022 platform text is Record only and carries no instrument here. — —
25 M13d standing School District 61 agreement — The slate's before- and after-school care and in-school supports sit with its school-board candidate, not with Kim, and are *we* in any case. — —
### 7 · Streets and mobility
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
26 M14/M16/M17/M18 cleanliness and the public realm **Close 2.0** YES 7–2 on the Pandora cleanup pilot: "A locking dumpster will be placed on the slip road alongside Pandora, and members of the street community will be paid a stipend to do waste collection in the area in a \$9,000 pilot project." Commits + comparable: a funded street-cleanliness instrument, but not M14's 48-hour graffiti standard or M17's extended sanitation hours. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/900-block-of-pandora-avenue-community-cleanup-pilot-program/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/900-block-of-pandora-avenue-community-cleanup-pilot-program/) vote 2 May 2025 per tracker, retrieved 2026-09-02
27 M19/M22/M38/M40–M42b mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38) **Close 2.0** YES 6–3 on the 2023–2027 financial plan's active-transportation allocation, on the argument that "bundling bike network construction with planned underground utility and road repaving projects reduces long-term construction costs." Commits + comparable: funds the protected-network build (M41), but no Vision Zero intersection programme, no safety-audit rule. M39 is struck and not scored. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/active-transportation-network-funding-2023-2027-financial-plan/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/active-transportation-network-funding-2023-2027-financial-plan/) vote 4 May 2023, retrieved 2026-09-02
28 M20b/M23b walking and transit the City controls — No sidewalk-gap inventory, crossing standard, transit priority line or published annual City transit position. Her bike-valet vote belongs to M20, which has no cell in the 55 (see Working notes). The slate's free-transit line is *we* and is not a City instrument in any case. — —
29 M24b/M25b accessibility and public washrooms **📋 Record** Her 2022 plank treating public bathrooms as transportation infrastructure is the plank the Program absorbed as M24b. 2022 campaign text counts as Record for an incumbent, shown not scored. No 2022–26 vote and no 2026 sentence on washroom spacing or an accessibility audit. [https://app.notion.com/p/3ade245ae5f381e495cafd4c31616fdd](https://app.notion.com/p/3ade245ae5f381e495cafd4c31616fdd) 2022 platform, logged 2026-09-01, retrieved 2026-09-02
30 M25 fix roads first — Road repaving appears only as the bundling rationale scored on row 27. One sentence, one measure. — —
### 8 · Policing and published safety
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
31 M28b business security cost-spreading — No position on an exposure-based business-security pilot. — —
32 M28d community paramedicine — No position on community paramedicine as a call-reduction instrument. — —
33 M29/M29b VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force) **📋 Record** Three named votes, none of them on this cell's instrument. NO on the \$62.27M 2024 VicPD provisional budget, 6–3, on concern about "over-indexing city revenues into policing at the expense of social services, affordable housing, and harm-reduction initiatives." NO on police staffing, 7–2: "83% of public submissions regarding policing explicitly opposed a police budget increase." YES 5–4 to cut the VicPD request by roughly \$344,000, reducing four new officers to two. **Shown, not scored:** M29 is the Esquimalt cost-share formula and M29b is a convened regional review. She has taken no position on either. Funding level is adjacent, and adjacency is not a source. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/victoria-police-budget-2024/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/victoria-police-budget-2024/) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/victoria-police-staffing/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/victoria-police-staffing/) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/reduction-to-proposed-police-officer-hiring/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/reduction-to-proposed-police-officer-hiring/) votes 26 Jan 2024, 27 Feb 2025, 4 Mar 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
34 M30 smart LED lights, no surveillance — No position on smart streetlighting or on the no-cameras rule. — —
35 M31/M31b/M31c/M32 safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target **Partial 1.0** YES 8–1 adopting the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan. Commits, but neither instrument: M31c's demand is to retrofit that plan into a performance contract with five mandatory fields and quarterly outcome reporting. No dashboard, no published enforcement record, no crime-reduction target anywhere in her record. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/community-safety-well-being-plan/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/community-safety-well-being-plan/) vote 20 Jun 2025 per tracker, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 9 · Beauty as a public good
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
36 M43–M46b heritage and cultural venues **Close 2.0** YES 7–2 on the downtown cinema retention strategy: "Victoria to look at how to keep, attract movie theatres as Odeon goes on market," prompted by the Cineplex Odeon, "a fixture downtown since 1948," listed at \$8.5 million. Commits + comparable: a cultural-venue retention instrument, but not M46b's designated list, right of first refusal, permissive tax exemption or lease-bridge fund. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/downtown-movie-theatres-retention-strategy/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/downtown-movie-theatres-retention-strategy/) vote 19 Jun 2025, retrieved 2026-09-02
37 M45b/c pedestrianisation and the signature project — No position on Bastion Square or Government Street pedestrianisation, or on a resident-chosen referendum-approved signature project. Her Centennial Square vote belongs to M45, which has no cell in the 55 (see Working notes). — —
38 M47–M49 heritage incentives, lighting, parks — No position on waterfront walkways, heritage lighting hours or parks investment. — —
39 M50/M50b/M51/M52 culture, sport, and the arts funding floor **Close 2.0** YES 7–2 on a one-time \$175,000 grant from contingency for the Victoria Curling Club ice-plant replacement, supporters citing "a vital community hub serving thousands of members." Commits + comparable: a sport-facility capital instrument, but not M52's Royal Athletic Park restoration or M50b's arts funding floor. **Recused** on the FernFest grant, 9 May 2026. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/grant-for-victoria-curling-club-ice-plant/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/grant-for-victoria-curling-club-ice-plant/) · [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/grant-for-fernfest/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/grant-for-fernfest/) votes 5 Apr 2026 and 9 May 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 10 · A smaller scored Hall
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
40 M15 managed competition — No published position. Her disclosed Labour Council commitment concerned P3s, a different instrument from competitive testing of an in-house service. Absence of action is Record, not Opposed, and there is no action to show. — —
41 M65 rotating zero-based reviews **📋 Record** NO in Nov 2025 on reducing infrastructure funding "from \$5.5 million to \$4 million to help cap the city's property tax increase at 4%"; the tracker records that she "resists scaling back city investments and services to satisfy low property tax targets." On 7 May 2026 she also said "The benefit of this exercise this year … we actually did find places we could cut back reasonably." **Shown, not scored:** neither touches a rotating zero-based review of 200+ programmes, and the second line raises the topic without naming a goal or an action. Mentions does not resolve up. [https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/2026-budget-reductions/](https://votereadyvictoria.ca/voting-items/2026-budget-reductions/) · [https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/) vote 26 Nov 2025 / press 11 May 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
42 M67 quarterly performance dashboard — No position on a quarterly performance dashboard. — —
43 M68 overhead reduction by attrition — No position on administrative overhead or attrition. — —
44 M69 real-estate rationalisation — No position on rationalising City real-estate holdings. — —
45 M53/M53b/M53c GIS, AI consultation imagery, LIDAR — No position. — —
46 M53d published municipal AI standard — No position. — —
47 M54–M57 local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging — No position on local-tech procurement, an open data portal, public Wi-Fi or EV charging. — —
### 11 · Climate and trees as operations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
48 M58/M58b/M64b climate, district energy, seismic — Slate pillar "SAFE CLIMATE FOR ALL: A healthier, cooler and more resilient city," with heat pumps and green roofs, is *we*, held under Ruling 1. No Kim-owned climate sentence and no sourced vote on district energy or seismic resilience. — —
49 M59–M63 trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness — Slate commitment to "retain the urban tree canopy" is *we*, held under Ruling 1. No Kim-owned sentence on a canopy target, mode share, stormwater or emergency preparedness. — —
### 12 · Neighbourhoods and integrity
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
